memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They fashioned the breastpiece - the work of a skilled craftsman. They made it like the ephod: of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen. It was square - a span long and a span wide - and folded double." - Exod 39:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A square pouch, folded double, worn over the high priest's heart.

The doubling was practical — it created a pocket, and it made the fabric strong enough to bear the weight of twelve precious stones. But the placement is what matters most. This piece sat directly over the heart.

Israel was carried in two places whenever the high priest entered God's presence: on his shoulders and over his heart. Strength and affection together.

That is not a small thing. It is possible to carry responsibility for people without loving them — to serve a church, a family, or a team out of duty while the heart has quietly disengaged. God's design put the names in both places.

Paul wrote to the Philippians that he held them in his heart (Phil 1:7). Jesus, looking at a crowd, had compassion on them because they were harassed and helpless (Matt 9:36). The care came before the ministry.

Ask honestly whether the people you serve are on your shoulders only, or also over your heart.

And take comfort: your great High Priest does not merely bear your burdens as a duty. He is not unable to sympathise with our weaknesses (Heb 4:15). You are carried by One who feels.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there people you serve out of duty but no longer love?
2. Where has your heart quietly disengaged from something you still do?
3. What does it mean that Christ carries you over His heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart engaged where my hands are working. Thank You that You carry me with love, not just duty. Amen.
